items.title: Transpose (linear algebra)

items.title: Scalar (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: A scalar is an element of a field used in the definition of a vector space.

items.title: Orthonormality (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: A set of vectors is orthonormal when they are all unit vectors and are pairwise orthogonal.

items.title: Orthogonality (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: Two vectors u and v are orthogonal with respect to a bilinear form B when B(u,v) = 0.

items.excerpt: Rectangular arrangement of numbers or other mathematical objects.[6] A matrix is written A = (ai, j), where ai, j is the entry at row i and column j.

items.title: Linear transformation (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: A linear map whose domain and codomain are equal; it is generally supposed to be invertible.

items.title: Linear independence (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: Property of being not linearly dependent.[12]

items.title: Linear algebra (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. The branch of mathematics that deals with vectors, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations.

items.excerpt: A vector space with a quadratic form which has a null vector.

items.title: Isotropic vector (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: In a vector space with a quadratic form, a non-zero vector for which the form is zero.

items.title: Identity matrix (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: A diagonal matrix all of the diagonal elements of which are equal to $1$.[6]

items.title: Elementary matrix (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: Square matrix that differs from the identity matrix by at most one entry

items.title: Dual space (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: The vector space of all linear forms on a given vector space.[7]

items.title: Dot product (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: Given two vectors of the same length, the dot product is the sum of the products of their corresponding indices.

items.title: Coordinate vector (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: The tuple of the coordinates of a vector on a basis.

items.title: Bilinear form (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: On vector space V over field K, a bilinear form is a function $B:V\times V\to K$ that is linear in each variable.

items.title: Basis (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: In a vector space, a linearly independent set of vectors spanning the whole vector space.[2]

items.title: Affine combination (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: A linear combination in which the sum of the coefficients is 1.
